05_HIGHS_NATIVE_CAPABILITY_AUDIT: HiGHS C++ API documentation, highspy Python package documentation, HiGHS GitHub source

audit_document: # HiGHS is the underlying C++ solver used by scipy.optimize.milp.
# HiGHS also has its own direct Python binding: highspy (pip install highspy).
# These are two SEPARATE access paths to the same solver engine.
# This document audits what HiGHS itself supports

column3: Core HiGHS functionality. Used by scipy.optimize.milp. Documented and production-tested.
column5: Standard LP/MILP solving — the current POLARIS path.

audit_document: Multiple sequential MILP solves (Option A pattern)
column3: HiGHS can solve the same model multiple times with modified objective vectors. API: Highs.changeColCost() Highs.run(). Each call is an independent MILP solve.
column5: Option A implementation pattern: solve Stage 1 → lock objective → solve Stage 2 etc.

column3: After solving Stage k, the optimal value z_k* can be added as a new inequality constraint via Highs.addRow() before solving Stage k+1.
column5: Standard epsilon-constraint method. Mathematically equivalent to sequential objective-locking.

column3: HiGHS 1.5+ introduced experimental multi-objective LP (not MILP) support via the 'multi-objective' model type. As of HiGHS 1.x stable releases, native multi-objective for MILP is NOT documented as a stable production feature.
column5: Critical distinction: HiGHS multi-objective LP ≠ HiGHS multi-objective MILP. POLARIS uses MILP (binary variables). Multi-objective MILP via a single HiGHS call is not confirmed as a stable HiGHS feature.

audit_document: Lexicographic optimization via single API call
column3: No documented single-call lexicographic MILP API exists in HiGHS stable releases (1.x). Lexicographic optimization in HiGHS requires iterative sequential solves at the application layer.
column5: This was the key contested claim in prior governance documents.

column3: highspy provides direct Python access to HiGHS C++ API without scipy wrapper. Enables Highs() object model construction. NOT currently installed or used in POLARIS.
column5: pip install highspy; 'import highspy' — not present in POLARIS .venv as of audit date.

column3: HiGHS C++ API includes experimental multi-objective support in development branches. The stable highspy API exposes: setObjectiveSense() passLinearObjective() — these are single-objective setters. Multi-objective setters in stable highspy: not confirmed.
column5: Any claim that HiGHS natively supports multi-objective via a single API call requires version-specific evidence.

column3: HiGHS development roadmap mentions multi-objective but stable MILP multi-objective is not documented in HiGHS 1.5/1.6 release notes as a production feature.
column5: Governance-safe position: treat as unconfirmed until version-specific evidence is provided.

audit_document: Accessing HiGHS via scipy multi-objective extension
column3: scipy.optimize.milp wrapper does not pass multi-objective parameters to HiGHS regardless of HiGHS native capability.
column5: The scipy API layer is the binding constraint regardless of HiGHS native capability.

05_HIGHS_NATIVE_CAPABILITY_AUDIT: HiGHS capabilities vary by version. POLARIS uses HiGHS via scipy. The scipy version in use determines which HiGHS version is bundled. Without executing 'scipy.__version__' and checking the bundled HiGHS version, the exact HiGHS version in POLARIS cannot be confirmed from static analysis alone.

Would require: python3 -c 'import scipy; print(scipy.__version__)' then cross-reference scipy version to bundled HiGHS version. This is an EXECUTABLE command — not performed under this read-only audit.

Version dependency creates an open item: HiGHS multi-objective capability claims MUST be qualified by version. Generic 'HiGHS supports multi-objective' claims are not governance-grade without version evidence.
HiGHS natively supports sequential single-objective MILP solving (Option A pattern) via its own API.
HiGHS does NOT expose a confirmed stable single-call native lexicographic MILP API as of HiGHS 1.x stable releases.
HiGHS multi-objective LP support exists experimentally but multi-objective MILP (relevant to POLARIS binary variables) is not confirmed stable.
Accessing any HiGHS native multi-objective feature requires bypassing scipy.optimize.milp and using highspy or C++ API directly.
The current POLARIS implementation uses scipy.optimize.milp — it accesses HiGHS through the scipy wrapper only.
